#1 The connected components functor π0 ⁣:Top→Set\pi_0\colon {\mathrm{Top}} \to {\mathrm{Set}}π0​:Top→Set lifts through TotDisconnTop→Set\mathrm{TotDisconnTop} \to {\mathrm{Set}}TotDisconnTop→Set, giving π0(X)\pi_0(X)π0​(X) the quotient topology coming from the natural map X→π0(X)X\to \pi_0(X)X→π0​(X). One can also define a pro-set version of π0(X)\pi_0(X)π0​(X) by taking the diagram π0pro(X)\pi_0^{\mathrm{pro}}(X)π0pro​(X) with objects the surjective continuous maps q ⁣:X→Sqq\colon X\to S_qq:X→Sq​ where SqS_qSq​ is a discrete space, and maps the obvious commutative triangles. The limit of this diagram in Top\mathrm{Top}Top is a pro-discrete space, a subspace of the topological product ∏qSq\prod_q S_q∏q​Sq​. As such it is a Hausdorff totally disconnected space. I imagine some loss of information has happened in passing from the pro-set to the limit (since the limit functor from pro-sets to spaces is apparently not full; at least the version for locales is not). Here are some obvious questions:

  • by the universal property for π0(X)\pi_0(X)π0​(X), there is a map π0(X)→lim⁡π0pro(X)\pi_0(X) \to \lim\pi_0^{\mathrm{pro}}(X)π0​(X)→limπ0pro​(X). Is this map the Hausdorffification?

  • Is π0(X)\pi_0(X)π0​(X) always Hausdorff? (There are totally disconnected spaces that aren’t)

  • Does π0(X)\pi_0(X)π0​(X) contain the ‘same information’ as π0pro(X)\pi_0^{\mathrm{pro}}(X)π0pro​(X)?

  • Can we recover the space π0(X)\pi_0(X)π0​(X) from π0pro(X)\pi_0^{\mathrm{pro}}(X)π0pro​(X)? (probably not)

content: #2 One could think of this in the same light as Clausen and Scholze’s “Condensed mathematics”, which is done working in sheaves over the pro-étale site of the point, or equivalently small sheaves on the category of extremally disconnected spaces with the extensive pretopology.

content: #5 So here is some progress: lim⁡π0pro(X)\lim \pi_0^{\mathrm{pro}}(X)limπ0pro​(X) is zero-dimensional Hausdorff, and there are continuous maps π0(X)→π0quasi(X)→lim⁡π0pro(X)\pi_0(X) \to \pi_0^{\mathrm{quasi}}(X) \to \lim\pi_0^{\mathrm{pro}}(X)π0​(X)→π0quasi​(X)→limπ0pro​(X), where the middle space is that of quasi-components, and is totally separated (such spaces are equal to their own π0quasi\pi_0^{\mathrm{quasi}}π0quasi​). I think the second map is injective, but not an embedding in general. The first map is surjective, but not injective in general. There are also Hausdorff totally separated spaces that aren’t zero-dimensional.

content:
#6 This reminds me somewhat of what Eduardo Dubuc was doing in the late 1990s. He was if I remember correctly using locales however.Ieke Moerdijk also worked on this sort of thing. Something along was published as `Localic Galois theory’ by Dubuc in Advances, in 2003 although that was going off in another direction.

May I ask why you want to bother with taking the limit as pro-sets work better and taking the limit does destroy information? Of course the answer may just be `curiosity’!

content: #7 Complete curiosity. I guess the main question I was wondering is whether the pro-set version has the same information as the topological space of connected components. Certainly the limit of the pro-set has less information, but it’s not even clear how one would sensibly phrase a statement of this sort.

content: #8 One could also consider the limit of the pro-set in the category of locales. This would potentially give another invariant. I saw this on the lab somewhere, but I can’t find it again! It said on the page that the limit functor wasn’t full, so likely there is loss of information there as well.
